title: Relative pseudo-coherence is detected on jointly surjective etale charts
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pullback and tensor use K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a locally finite type morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme $S$ [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, and fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. Define $K$ to be $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$ when for every commutative square $U\to V$, $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ with $U,V$ schemes and the vertical maps etale, the corresponding object $K|_U$ of the scheme derived category is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. The corresponding scheme object is obtained from etale restriction by the equivalence [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]. Let $I$ be a set, let $\{u_i:U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale maps from schemes, let $v_i:V_i\to Y$ be etale maps from schemes, and let $a_i:U_i\to V_i$ satisfy $v_i\circ a_i=g\circ u_i$. Then $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$ if and only if, for every $i$, $K|_{U_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V_i$. Consequently if these scheme restrictions are pseudo-coherent relative to their $V_i$ for every $i$, then $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$, meaning $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$. Covers may depend on $m$; no finite covering or global cohomological bound is required.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, equivalence of (1) and (2), applied to the disjoint union of the covering squares; Definition 0CSY, definition-relative-pseudo-coherence.

proof.text: If $K$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$, apply the defining universal quantifier to each given square $(U_i,V_i)$. This proves the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: For the converse fix an arbitrary test square $a:U\to V$ over $g$, with $U\to X$ and $V\to Y$ etale. For each $i$ form $W_i=U_i\times_XU$ and $T_i=V_i\times_YV$. These are schemes because the arrows to $X,Y$ are representable etale. Write $p_i:W_i\to U_i$ and $q_i:W_i\to U$ for the projections. The maps $q_i$ form a jointly surjective etale family; $p_i$ and both projections from $T_i$ are etale. The pair $(a_i p_i,a q_i)$ defines $b_i:W_i\to T_i$. Etale composition makes $W_i\to X$ and $T_i\to Y$ etale. The chart test for local finite type applied to $g$ therefore gives local finite type of $a_i,a,b_i,W_i\to V_i$, and $W_i\to V$.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: Let $E_i,E_U,E_{W_i}$ be the corresponding scheme derived objects of $K|_{U_i},K|_U,K|_{W_i}$. Etale restriction is exact and preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by the chart-calculus statement. The etale-to-Zariski equivalence puts these objects in the scheme $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. Its pullback comparison and the associative pullback comparison identify $Lp_i^*E_i\cong E_{W_i}\cong Lq_i^*E_U$: both maps to $X$ equal $u_i p_i=u q_i$. These are derived isomorphisms, not only cohomology identifications.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: By hypothesis $E_i$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V_i$. Etale means flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus $\{\mathrm{id}_{U_i},p_i:W_i\to U_i\}$ is an fppf covering, since its identity member already covers $U_i$. Apply the forward implication of the fixed-base scheme fppf-descent theorem to this covering, the locally finite type map $a_i:U_i\to V_i$ and the quasi-coherent object $E_i$. It gives $E_{W_i}\cong Lp_i^*E_i$ $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V_i$. No surjectivity of $p_i$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: For each projection $t:T_i\to V_i$ or $t:T_i\to V$, etaleness gives flatness and local finite presentation. The flat-lfp structure theorem makes $\mathcal O_{T_i}[0]$ pseudo-coherent relative to the respective target. Apply the composition theorem first to $W_i\xrightarrow{b_i}T_i\to V_i$ and then to $W_i\xrightarrow{b_i}T_i\to V$. Its local-finite-type hypotheses for $b_i$ and the composites were checked in step 2; the projections are locally of finite type since they are etale. It yields the chain of equivalences: $E_{W_i}$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V_i$ if and only if it is so relative to $T_i$, if and only if it is so relative to $V$. Hence all $Lq_i^*E_U$ have the property relative to $V$.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: The family $\{q_i:W_i\to U\}$ is jointly surjective etale, hence an fppf covering. Apply the reverse implication of scheme fppf descent with base $V$, source $U$, complex $E_U$ and degree $m$. The local finite type of $a$ and quasi-coherence of $E_U$ were checked in steps 2 and 3. Step 5 supplies every pullback hypothesis. Thus $E_U$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $V$. Since the test square was arbitrary, this is precisely the required universal condition on $K$.

source.place: Tag 0CSX, lemma-qcoh-relative-pseudo-coherence-characterize, proof of (2) implies (1), applied componentwise; Definition 0CSY

proof.text: Finally fix any integer $m$. If every given chart restriction is pseudo-coherent relative to its base, its defining condition supplies $m$-pseudo-coherence there. Apply the equivalence just proved and then quantify over $m$. The same reasoning permits a separate covering for each $m$: neither the fixed-$m$ proof nor this quantification chooses a finite subcover or a uniform cohomological bound. If the indexing family is empty, joint surjectivity forces $X$ empty, and the fppf-descent statement on the empty test schemes gives the same conclusion.
